claims.text: The proposed method uses machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on a limited set of ab initio molecular-dynamics data.
The machine-learned potentials can capture vibrational entropy.
The machine-learned potentials can capture anharmonicity.
The machine-learned potentials can capture electron–vibration coupling.
Combining the potentials with thermodynamic integration or enhanced sampling can compute solid- and liquid-phase free energies.
Near melting, vibrational entropy and electron–vibration effects are significant.
The surrogate potential retains relevant structural details, including vibrational spectra and anharmonic corrections, in both solid and liquid phases.
Strategically sampling phase-space regions important to vibrational and anharmonic contributions allows the potential to reproduce solid–liquid free-energy differences.
Using the surrogate substantially reduces the number of expensive ab initio molecular-dynamics runs required.
The surrogate preserves the fidelity of phase free energies.
The surrogate preserves the fidelity of derived melting points and latent heats.
For elemental and binary materials, the approach will reduce computational cost by at least one order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
For elemental and binary materials, the approach will reduce computational cost by at least one order of magnitude relative to TOR-TILD.
The approach will provide accuracy comparable to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD for melting temperatures and fusion-related properties.
Initial applicability is restricted to elemental and simple binary systems whose relevant solid and liquid configuration spaces are adequately represented in the training data.
The method is restricted to temperatures near the melting point and to regimes validated against ab initio or TOR-TILD calculations.
Efficacy for multicomponent high-entropy systems remains unvalidated.
Extreme anharmonicity may require additional training data or methodological changes.

A decisive benchmark compares solid–liquid free-energy differences, melting temperature, latent heat, and computational resource use against full ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD on the same system.
Failure to attain benchmark-comparable thermodynamic accuracy or at least a tenfold computational-cost reduction falsifies the hypothesis.
